title: 1 Look Line Last Layer (1LLLL)
summary: 1LLLL, an abbreviation for 1-Look Line Last Layer, is a subset to meant for solving the last layer (1 look) in 17 algorithms. In order to bring the number of cases for the last layer down to 18, (including the solved case) some F2L influence is needed. Edge orientation needs to be solved before F2L-1, so that the last layer algorithm count goes to 493 (ZBLL). After that, the last F2L pair is solved along with 3 adjacent last layer pieces (2 corners, 1 edge).

summary: 1 Look Last Layer means completing the last layer using only one look. On the 3x3, currently ZBLL is the only known practical system for achieving a 1-look last layer, but other experimental approaches such as 1-look 2-alg (such as M-CELL) may have potential. In 2022, Eduardo Silva Damasceno became the first person to ever learn all 1LLL algorithms.

title: 2 holes
summary: 2 Holes is a 3x3 speedsolving method proposed by V Achyuthan in 2021. It relies heavily on block building and intuitiveness. The move count for the beginner version with some experience in block building and Full COLL will be around 49.5 moves. The intermediate version averages around the same movecount but has higher TPS potential than the beginner version if you learn L5EP. The advanced version has around 662 algorithms. 630 For 2 holes CLL, 16 for L5EP, and 16 for RL5EP.

title: 2GB
summary: 2GB, short for 2-Generator Blockbuilding, is similar to RUP/PRUM/RUPM method by Tsung-Yen Wu, and also Heise. But unlike all other Blockbuilding methods (except Heise), 2GB method can utilize blockbuilding techniques throughout the solve from start to finish. And unlike all other 2-generator methods (except RUP/PRUM/RUPM), it is possible to solve the cube with 2GB method without using any predetermined or memorized Last Layer algorithms.

summary: 2GLL (short for 2-Generator Last Layer) is a subset of ZBLL, when all the LL edges are oriented, it solves the LL in 1 of 493 algorithms. 2GLL consists of 85 cases (including solved) that orient the corners and permute the edges, i.e. exactly the ZBLL cases that can be solved by a 2-generator algorithm (using only 2-Gen moves, usually R and U moves). 2GLL is very useful when used with a system that permutes LL corners and orients LL edges before or during the last layer.

title: 2GR Method
summary: 2GR (2 generator reduction) is an advanced speedsolving method that reduces the cube to the <R,U> subgroup, allowing for a very ergonomic F2L step and an 84-algorithm 1-look LL. 1. EOPair: create a 2x1x1 corner-edge pair at DBL-DL while orienting all the edges. 2. CPLine: complete a 3x1x1 line on LD while reducing the remaining 6 corners to <R,U>. 3. Block: expand the line into a 3x2x2 block. 5. 2GLL: complete the last layer in 1 look. Relatively low move count (comparable to Roux).

title: 2oux
summary: 2oux is a variant of the Roux method that aims for a more algorithmic approach to the last 10 pieces of the normal Roux method. Instead of using 42 CMLLs to solve the corners and then solve LSE intuitively, 2oux orients all of the pieces using roughly 170 algs and then permutes all of them using somewhere between 300-500 algs. Same as Roux FB. Solve a 1x2x3 block on one side of the cube Same as Roux SB. Solve another 1x2x3 on the other side of the cube using rRUM moves.

title: 3-Color Cube Method
summary: The 3-Color Cube method is a unique solving method developed completely independently by Michael Feather in 1980. The method name (not to be confused with Feather's algorithm) is derived from the 3-Color Cube, which is a Rubik's Cube having tri-color scheme that uses the same color on opposite faces. There are 2 steps for a 3-Color Cube and 4 steps for a 6-Color Cube with the same set of algorithms (which can be found in the External Links section below if needed).

Step 1: Solve the middle layer using the commutators R U' R and L' U L Step 2: OBS, Orient the puzzle so that on both opposite sides are either yellow OR white. The way you do this is with 2-look OLL on both sides. You may encounter OBS parity on this step.

APLL is divided into around 7 subsets (except PLL, and still developing), and APLL has around 454 cases. The subset name indicates which corners are involved in the permutation.

summary: The goal of Brekreney's Fun Time is to reduce the cube to a state wherein four J-permutations separated by z rotations will solve the cube. This desired state is referred to by the method as the QJ pattern This intuitive step involves block building a green Brek-Block on the D layer, and then a blue Brek-Block on the U layer. Brek-Blocks are a type of pseudoblocks used specifically for the BFT method. This step solves the BL edge while preserving the two blocks built in the previous step.

summary: CEOR is a Rubik's Cube method designed for use in one-handed speedsolving. It can be seen as the counterpart to LEOR because, aside from the early corner permutation aspect, the steps are the same. Since the early 2000's CEOR has been created multiple times by different proposers and under different names. Because of this, it was decided to group all of the proposals into a single method. The name CEOR was created to match LEOR and the C is short for Corner Permutation (CP).

Then, you solve the last layer in two steps. Instead of solving it by doing OLL then PLL, you solve it by first doing CLL (Corners of the last layer) and then, doing ELL (Edges of the Last Layer). summary: CFOP (Cross, F2L, OLL, PLL, pronounced C-F-O-P or C-fop) is a 3x3 speedsolving method proposed by several cubers around 1981. It is also known as the Fridrich Method after its popularizer, Jessica Fridrich. In part due to Fridrich's publication of the method on her website in 1995, CFOP has been the most dominant 3x3 speedcubing method since around 2000, with it and its variants used by the vast majority of the top speedcubers such as Feliks Zemdegs, Max Park, Sebastian Weyer, Mats Valk, etc.

title: CLL
summary: Note: This page is about 2x2x2 CLL. For the 3x3x3 CLL see CLL algorithms (3x3x3) CLL (Corners of the Last Layer) is an algorithm set that solves the last layer corners, generally on a 2x2x2 Cube, in one algorithm, or on higher order cubes when all layers below the last layer have been completely solved. Not to be confused with COLL that is an abbreviation for exactly the same approach except COLL preserves LL edge orientation on a 3x3.

title: CLLEF
summary: Corners Last Layer [and] Edge Flip is a subset of OLLCP. CLLEF is similar to COLL in that it orients and permutes last layer corners simultaneously. However, instead of preserving LL edge orientation the algorithms flip all last-layer edges, leaving only edge permutation (EPLL). This would be used as an alternative to OLL/PLL in a regular Fridrich solve, where the OLL case has no oriented edges.

summary: The CML-Method (Corner-Middle-Layer-Method) is a speedsolving method created in 2020. It's predecessor was the Waterman Method, but CML uses far less algorithms and is effitiently enough to be a speedcubing method.

title: CMLL
summary: Solving of corner orientation and permutation, without regard to the M-slice edges or U layer corners. This is Step 3 of the Roux Method. Similar to CLL. It will always have a lower movecount than COLL. One suggestion for improving this step is to use it in order to influence the orientation or permutation of edges in LSE (in particular avoiding 6-flips and encouraging EO skips or Arrow cases).

title: COALL
summary: COALL (Corner Orientation And Last Layer) is an experimental 3x3 method, a ZB variant that orients the last-layer corners when inserting the last F2L pair (COLS). It has no known user. Orienting the corners first, rather than the edges like in normal ZB, has the advantage of requiring less algorithms (111 total compared to ZB's 300). To solve using COALL, solve the cross and three F2L slots using any method.

title: COLL
summary: COLL (short for Corners of Last Layer) is a 3x3x3 last layer substep in the CxLL group that solves (orients and permutes) the last layer corners while preserving the last layer edge orientation, leaving only edge permutation (EPLL). It is principally used as a last layer for ZZ (as it has a higher skip chance and is nicer for OH than OCLL/PLL when used with EPLL) or an add-on to Fridrich, when the last layer edges are already oriented after F2L. COLL has 42 cases including mirrors (24 without).

title: CPEOLL
summary: CPEOLL, corner permutation and edge orientation of the last layer, is an experimental method for the last layer. It solves edge orientation and corner permutation, while not preserving corner orientation. This then leaves edge permutation and corner orientation to be solved, which can be achieved using 2GLL, that only uses R and U moves. CPEOLL was previously used to refer to OLLCP-A, but this usage has changed.

title: CR†
summary: CR† is a revised, simplified and improved version of Cardan Reduction. Recognition is easier with CR† than CR and the last substep is L3C, easier than CR3 substep. (CR1) F2L-1 + EO cube state to F2L-1C + EO + 2x1x1 block cube state : Insert FR edge and create a U-layer 2x1x1 block. (CR2†) F2L-1 + EO cube state to L3C cube state : Solve the 2x1x1 pair, all edges, and last D corners. Algorithms for the 2nd substep (CR2†) can be found here.

title: Columns First Methods
summary: Columns first is a group of methods for the 3x3x3 cube that in some way build four columns of three pieces each, two adjacent corners and the and the edge between them, as the first steps. Columns are most often aligned top to bottom but two more directions are possible. These methods can be relatively fast, effective and easy but there are few cubers who use columns as their main method. Solve 4 middle layer edges using the LBL alg and its mirror.

title: Corner Orientation
summary: Corner Orientation, abbreviated CO, the orientation of a cube's corners. There are three possible corner cubie orientations. CO is a substep in many methods.

title: Corner Permutation of the Last Layer

infobox.name: Corner Permutation of the Last Layer

summary: Corner Permutation of the Last Layer, abbrevaited CPLL, permutes the corners of the last layer without affecting anything else. It has four cases, one of wich is the H perm + U2 and the other are Aa, Ab and E perm

title: Corners First
summary: Corners First methods, abbreviated as CF, are speedcubing methods that solve all of the corners (relative to each other) before anything else. There are not very many serious CF solvers for 3x3x3 these days, but CF methods are relatively easy to invent and were very popular in the 1980s. At least in theory, CF methods exist for all puzzles with corners, although for many puzzles (such as big cubes) they are impractical for speedsolving.

title: Doorspray
summary: Doorspray is a variation of the Layer by Layer method similar to the common beginners method. The creator describes it as "heavily optimized LBL", using algorithms to solve the first layer, second layer, and third layer. This involves solving a side of the cube on U and is completely intuitive This uses PLL and Parity PLL for 3x3 to solve the first layer completely, then do a rotation to put the layer on D if necessary.

title: Doug Li Method
summary: The Doug Li Method is a Rubik's cube speedsolving method developed by Doug Li. Complete the F2L minus one edge on the first layer. The way Doug Li completed this step was to have the F2L as the top two layers. So the missing edge would be on the U layer. The modern convention is to solve the F2L on the bottom two layers, so that would mean that the user builds the F2L minus one D layer edge. Doug Li had his own set of steps for building the F2L minus one edge. They are shown below.

title: Duplex method
summary: Duplex is an experimental speedcubing method that aims to produce better solutions than traditional two look last layer methods.

title: E2CR2
summary: E2CR2 (Edge orientation + Left block, 2x2x3, Corner permutation, Right block, 2GLL) is a method which could be seen as a mix between ZZ and Roux, although due to effectively solving an EO223 in the beginning, it also shares similarities with Petrus and LEOR. E2CR2's ergonomics are excellent both for 2-handed solving and One-handed solving after the EOFB stage. After the EOFB step the cube can be solved only using r, R, U and D moves.

title: ECBL
summary: ECBL is a columns first method where you solve Edge Orientation while solving all the pairs and ending with L5EP. This method was invented as a revision to the FECE method. Orient all the edges on the cube ZZ-like while solving all the pairs. This would lead to better ergonomics (maybe) while setting up the “columns first” idea. The recommended way to do this is by inspecting EO and the first 2 pairs (on left), and then doing the last 2 right pairs.

title: ECBLv2
summary: ECBLv2 is a remake of the ECBL method. ECBLv2 started as only a variant of ECBL but slowly grew into its own method. In this step you solve EO and the 4 d-layer pairs except 2 of these pairs can be swapped diagonally. It is impossible to have 2 pairs swapped adjacently as that would mean EO is unsolved. This step is solved by first solving EO and any 2 d-pairs onto the left, and then solving the remaining right pairs. This step averages 19.3 STM and is entirely intuitive.

title: ECCE
summary: In this step you must solve edge orientation and a 2x2x3 block in the dl position of the cube. This can be done in many ways. You could do FBEO and then solve DFDB while preserving edge orientation. You could also solve the dL 1x2x3 block and then do EOStripe like in LEOR method. The last way you could do this is first making a 2x2x3 on left and then do edge orientation with algorithms.

title: ECP Method
summary: ECP is a method that was invented for the Method Development Competition January 2021 by team Kübirz. It is designed to use inspection to do an intuitive step, in order to get to algorithmic steps as quickly as possible. Experience with ZZ/CFOP last layers, Roux’s L4E, and ZZ’s Edge Orientation step are highly recommended. 1. Solve EO and build a face on the D layer.

title: ELL

There are 29 cases in ELL, of these are three pure flips, four are EPLL and six cases are 3-cycles (besides the two in EPLL), all useful also for other methods, like BLD.

title: Edge Supertwist Method
summary: The Edge SuperTwist method, EST is a 3x3 method that solves the cube in permutations. In the basic, Edge Supertwist Method, the solver finishes the cube by first solving the E layer, then permuting the first layer, then the last layer, then orienting all the corners, then finishing by orienting all the edges. This is a uncommon method for newer cubers to discover on their own.

title: Edges First
summary: Edges first, or just EF, is a method where all edges of the cube are solved before the corners. EF is not well suited for advanced speedsolving, the first step is very easy but the corners needs a unplesant number of moves to be solved after that in most cases.

This is done the same way as APB, first you solve a Roux 1x2x3 block on the left. Then you solve the DF and DB edges using Rru generator moves. It is quite ergonomic and movecount efficient.

title: FECE
summary: FECE is a method where the first 2 steps are made to be easy intuitive steps while finishing with algorithms for the final 3 steps. This could be beneficial due to easy planning during inspection of the first three corners and a smooth transition to the algorithmic steps. Might have high TPS but one down side that might exist is the abundance of S and E moves which might be tricky to finger trick but will get better over time.

title: FLFL Method
summary: The FLFL method is a 3x3x3 method where 3 corners in the first layer and all edges are oriented and permuted (F2L-1CE and LFE) without the use of algorithms. Once the final first-layer corner is solved (while preserving the edges) through the use of FLLC, then the puzzle is in a state where it can put into a solved state using an L4C algorithm. Inspired by Ryan Heise's Method and Bernd Bruegmann's Y-Move Method. F2L-1CE: First Two Layers minus One Corner-Edge Pair (No algorithms required).

title: Fail Method
summary: Fail Method, (also Face By Face or just FBF), a method that solves the cube face by face. This method is very slow and inefficient (and difficult too), and definitely not recommended for speedcubing. First you complete one face using intuition (or trial and error, if you aren't familiar with the cube). Then, you try to do another one, in the same way. If you manage that, the next and last step is to do a third face.

summary: FreeFOP (Free F2L, OLL, PLL) is a 3x3x3 speedsolving method based on CFOP. FreeFOP was proposed and posted on the SpeedSolving Forums by Thom Barlow on 18 June 2010. The person who created the term "FreeFOP" was Michael Gottlieb while Barlow spoke about the method in a chatroom on StrangePuzzle.com (now offline). Solve the first two layers F2L however you wish.

But unlike all other Columns first and Corners first methods (except SSC), HSC solves Corner orientation and Belt edges orientation simultaneously.

title: Hahn Method
summary: The Hahn Method is a blockbuilding and intuitive keyhole based method. First build a 2x2x3 block then add one edge at the bottom and one edge at the left side. Next use the keyhole for placing every edge and two corners into position. The last step is to solve the remaining corners with L4C.

The alternative is Hall-2 which has a more block building approach and slightly less moves but has worse algorithms. 1. F2L-1-Solve your F2L with any method without the FRD pair. 2. OLTP-Orient the Last 10 Pieces (5 corners , 5 edges) with one algorithm.

title: Heise method
summary: The Heise method, invented by Ryan Heise, is an intuitive method which requires no algorithms. It uses extremely few moves, but it may be difficult to get fast times using this method. Create four 1x2x2 blocks (also called Heise blocks), making sure that one color appears on none of the blocks. This color will be the color of the last layer. Note that these blocks do not necessarily have to be paired together when they are built. One of these blocks should be just two centers and an edge.

title: Hexagonal Francisco
summary: The Hexagonal Francisco method is a variation of the Triangular Francisco 3x3 speedsolving method invented by Michael Gottlieb. It was created by Andrew Nathenson, also known by his YouTube alias ColorfulPockets, with the help of Henry Helmuth. 1. Build a hexagon and place it on DB. A hexagon is a 1x2x3 block + a corner in the DFL slot. 2. Solve the E layer. You can use many strategies, including Keyhole. 3 or 4. Simultaneously orient the U-layer corners while inserting the last corner.

title: Human Thistlethwaite Algorithm
summary: The Human Thistlethwaite Algorithm (abbreviated to HTA) is a human-usable version, proposed by Ryan Heise, of the Thistlethwaite's algorithm. The solution is broken down into exactly the same basic steps of the computer Thistlethwaite algorithm, but each step in the human version is broken down into further sub-steps to make it managable for a human solver.

title: Iacob method
summary: Iacob is a speedcubing method invented by Iacob Razvan in February 2023. It relies heavily on algorithms but also on intuition, making this a likable and fast method. 1. Solve EO and build a pseudo face on the D layer without the DFR corner (EoFace-1C) 3. Insert the DFR corner while orienting the top layer corners (CLS) 4. Fix parities and permute the last & first layers.

title: Keyhole F2L
summary: Keyhole First Two Layers or Keyhole F2L, sometimes named working corner, is a method that solves, normally, the first two bottom layers of the 3x3x3 cube. It is an efficient method for inserting mid-layer edges in the 3x3x3 LBL method. Its a slight advancement on the basic LBL method, because it requires fewer moves, as well as more intuition. After the bottom layer cross, only three bottom layer corners are solved.

title: L2L4
summary: L2L4 (Last 2 Layers, the 4th proposal) is a 3x3 speedsolving method invented by Duncan Dicks in the 1990s. L2Lk (Last 2 Layers, as proposed by Stachu Korick) is an alternate 3x3 speedsolving method developed in late 2010 through 2011. L2L4 was conceived by Duncan Dicks, who first posted about a series of L2L strategies (L2L1 through L2L4) on the Yahoo! speedsolving group in 2004. Duncan found many algorithms, while Richard Carr also provided several.

title: L5C
summary: L5C (Last Five Corners) is a step used in various methods which solves five corners that remain unsolved. Much like CxLL, L5C comprises multiple variants with each one differing depending on the pieces that are to be preserved on the rest of the puzzle. One method which uses L5C contains the steps of 1x2x3 on the left, 1x2x2 on the right, L5C, then L7E. The algorithms for this version of L5C were first developed by James Straughan.

title: L5EOP
summary: L5EOP, last five edges orientation and placement of the last first layer edge, is an experimental method for the 3x3x3 cube that is an alternative to L5E. In L5E the last five edges are first oriented without minding the permutation for the last first layer edge (normally the FD edge), then all five are permuted together. That makes 5 algorithms for L5EO (orientation) and 16 for L5EP (permutation).

title: LEOR
summary: LEOR (Left block, EOStripe, Right block) is a method which could be seen as a mix between ZZ and Roux, although due to effectively solving an EO223 in the beginning, it also shares similarities with Petrus. LEOR allows for ergonomic steps while also offering a low movecount. FB/LB: Build a 1x2x3 Block on the left side of the cube. EOStripe: Orient all edges while simultaneously solving DF and DB. SB/RB: Build a second 1x2x3 block on the right side of the cube.

title: LLEF
summary: LLEF (Last Layer Edges First) is a variation of ELL (Edges of the Last Layer) that ignores corners is easier to solve; it uses both fewer moves and has fewer cases than what is the 'normal ELL'. This variation is useful for a 2-look method that solves corners last (see L4C).

title: LMCF
summary: The LMCF Method, or Low Movecount Corners First, was invented by Eric Fattah. It is an improved version of the Corners First Method. Because of its low movecount, the method can easily be used to get sub-10 singles with only 4-5 TPS. 1. Solve the corners with full EG. Make sure the centers are solved relative to the corners. 2. Transition Phase - This step doesn't require any algorithms, but it is very important.

title: LSFB Method
summary: LSFB, or Light Slice Fire Blocks (a parody name of SSC) is a method that was originally planned to be submitted for the January-February 2021 Method Development Competition by Team Kübirz (with a majority of the work done by [Ryan Kennelly]), but was later scrapped in favour of ECP Method. It has an extremely low number of algorithms, making it beginner friendly, while also introducing the solver to advanced concepts like EO.

title: Last Four Corners
summary: Last four corners, abbreviated L4C (or 4LC), is a method that solves the last layer corners preserving all the rest, a sub group of ZBLL and ZZLL. L4C is and is not a method in the CxLL group, not because it has twice the number of cases as all the other methods of the group (42/84). For a 2-look last layer this is preceeded with LLEF (ELL-CLL).

title: Last Three Corners
summary: Last three corners, abbrevaited L3C (or 3LC), is a method that solves three of the last layer corners preserving all the rest, a sub group of L4C, ZBLL and ZZLL. Usage: besides L4C, CxLL, ZBLL and ZZLL it is useful for FMC and the 3-cycles are nice for Freestyle BLD.  L3C is the final stage in the Snyder Method. Ryan Heise explains an intuitive approach to solve the last three corners. The group have 27 cases including solved, 3*3 orientations and 3 permutations.

summary: Layer-By-Layer, or normally only LBL is a group of methods that solves the cube in layers. In the basic, beginner LBL method, the solver finishes the layers one at a time: the first layer edges, then corners, then the second layer edges, and finally the last layer. This is a common method for new cubers to discover on their own. In more advanced LBL methods, you solve layers more efficiently or solve two layers at once.

title: Line
summary: Line is a 1LLL subset that solves for last layer cases which have a correctly oriented 1x1x3 block.

summary: M-CELL is a 2-algorithm 1-LLSLL method that can be added on to various methods as a final step it has one algorithm for solving L5C and one for L5E. Each are commutators meaning that neither affects the other so both can be recognised at the same time and executed one after each other without having to rerecognise.

title: MGLS
summary: The Makisumi-Garron Last Slot (abbreviation MGLS) is a method for solving the final F2L slot while simultaneously orienting the last layer, invented by Shotaro Makisumi in 2006 and later developed by Lucas Garron.

title: Maritan method
summary: This method uses algorithms that allow you to proceed with a layer by layer or corner first approach independently. It does not aim to be a fast method of resolution, but since it is intuitive and equipped with few algorithms to memorize, it is more suitable for beginners who want to understand the dynamics of rotation and operation of the few algorithms used. First Step - Position and orient the corners of the first layer. Second step - Arrange and orient edges of first and second layer.

By using the inverse sexy move and its mirror it is possible to significantly reduce the amount of intuition required in each step. Between applications of inverse sexy move (or its mirror) the user only needs to decide on at most one intuitive move. Solving the cross and the the final layer alignments are the only exceptions to this.

Pseudo RB - Solve the right block with the corners unpermuted.

Unlike M-CELL both LS and LL are solved simultaneously with 1 algorithm. It's also boasted as a 5LS Method or a 5-Look Solve Method meaning the entire cube is done with 5 looks. (1 look= 1 recognition, 1 algortithm) Solve any 3rd pair and 3 LL edges relative to each other (My Last/3rd Slot) The My Last/3rd Slot is divided into their respective 60 F2L cases.

title: N3DR
summary: This is meant to be a way to speedsolve the Domino Reduction state on a 3x3x3, so it requires the cube to already be at said state. It has no relation to Fewest Moves Challenge event. The rule is:  use only legal moves to solve the cube from that state, those are all moves that are possible on a real 2x3x3, generators: <R2,U,D,L2,F2,B2,M2,S2,E,Rw2,Lw2,Fw2,Bw2> This rule is not objectively optimal in speedsolving terms. Build a 2x2x3 block on the left of the cube, this step is done intuitively.

title: NMLL
summary: NMLL is an LL method to be used along with matching or non-matching blocks in methods that orient edges early (such as ZZ or Petrus).  First, the colors that match the L and R centers are separated to opposite sides of the U-layer facing away from the U center.  Then, the pieces are permuted into their correct places. Recognition Guide Guide for recognizing Step 2. Improved algorithms for step 2 by Vincent Trang

title: No More PLL
summary: The No More PLL Method is a 3x3 speedsolving method proposed by CriticalCubing in 2017. This method provides an alternate approach to CFOP while not being an handicap to traditional CFOP. You can use your CFOP techniques freely, but NMP provides alternate approach to Last Layer, finishing with 4c, instead of PLL. Solving this way, completely eliminates PLL and Diagonal Swap PLL's like N/V/Y/F which are considered bad and generally needs an extra alg to be learned which avoids these cases.

title: OC(P)ELL
summary: OC(P)ELL (not to be confused with Opposite Cross ELL) stands for Orient Corners (Permute) Edges Last Layer. This is a set of algorithms for solving last layer which orients the corners and permutes the edges simultaneously. The algorithms for this preserve last layer edge orientation, but not corner permutation. It is best used with a method which pre-orients the LL edges, such as ZZ, Petrus, VH or ZBLS. If used in this way, the final step to complete the last layer is CPLL.

title: OCLL
summary: Orient Corners of the Last Layer, abbreviated OCLL or OLL-C, is a last layer method that orients the corners preserving edge orientation but permutation for all LL-pieces is ignored. OCLL is a sub group of OLL. Following the usual naming system for cube methods this would be COLL, but that name has been used for a CxLL method since long ago.

summary: OLL (short for Orientation of the Last Layer) is a last-layer step for 2x2 (see OLL (2x2x2)) and 3x3 that orients all last-layer corners and edges in one step. It is the first last-layer step in many speedsolving methods, including the Fridrich Method. OLL is usually followed by PLL. Dot OLLs refer to the OLL cases with no edges oriented correctly, so named because the center sticker forms a lone dot of the last-layer color.

title: OLLCP
summary: Orientation of the Last Layer and Corner Permutation OLLCP is an experimental LL method which both orients the last layer and solves the corners. Thus after this step only EPLL remains. The price to get there however is a high algorithm count (300+). Only a very few number of people use the full set, but a number of people use the subsets COLL and CLLEF.

title: OLLCP-A
summary: OLLCP-A, corner permutation and edges orientation of the last layer, an experimental method for the 3x3x3 cube that permutes the last layer corners and orients the last layer edges preserving F2L. Orientation of Last Layer and Corner Permutation OLLCP-A is an experimental LL method which both orients the last layer edges and permutes the last layer corners when the corners are already oriented. Thus after this step only EPLL remains.

title: OPLL
summary: OPLL, also known as lazy ZBLL is a subset of the ZBLL last layer method that caan be solved with conjugate PLL's.  So no new algorithms need to be learned if you already know PLL (Conjugate is [A B A']). Please note that because not everyone uses the same PLL's, the first listed case may not work for you. Because of this, the PLL is listed inside the brackets, feel free to subsitute it. There may be some AUF's or rotations involved in certain cases which will be listed below.

title: Ofapel method
summary: The Ofapel Method is a "universal method" proposed by Guillaume Erbibou. It is considered universal in the sense that the 3x3x3 algs are the base for the 4x4x4 resolution which is the base for the 5x5x5 and so on. This method relates more and more on your understanding of the cube structure as you solve bigger cubes. For size beyond 5x5x5, you need to adapt all the algs learned from the smaller cube solves.

Variants of the orient first method are available in the external links below. The purpose of this method is to orient corners and edges to allow for an intuitive F2L and finishing the solve with PLL.

It is named after Victor Ortega, and is mostly popular today for being an intermediate 2x2 solving method. Victor Ortega is often credited for creating the method.  While it is true that Victor popularized the method, he cannot be said to have created it, similar to the naming dispute with the CFOP method.

It was made as a low movecount method with good ergonomics while keeping a manageable algorithm count(Most methods nowadays have about 400 algorithms) 1. 2x2x3 on Left - Solve a 2x2x3 block on the left. title: PCMS
summary: PCMS (pairs, CLL, M and S slices) is an advanced method for speedsolving using columns first, designed by Kenneth Gustavsson in late 2008. The method compromises between easy look ahead and low move count (slice metric), and the result is 'decent' for both parts. The first two steps of PCMS leave the cube in a very similar state to the first two steps of Roux method. CMSLL (42 algs), something between 2x2 CLL and CMLL (see CxLL).

title: PDQF Method
summary: PDQF, or Pseudo Domino Quadrangular Francisco, is an experimental method created in December 2019 by Rowan Fortier. It was completely forgotten about, until it was rediscovered, and then fully developed in August of 2020. PDQF is primarily based on Domino Reduction, the Belt Method, and a little bit of Quadrangular Francisco. 1. EOEdge (EOLine but with the BL & FL edges) 2a. Make a pseudo1x2x3 rectangle on the D face with the D color. Put this rectangle under the EoEdge 2b.

title: PEC
summary: PEC is a very efficient but algorithm-intensive method which is a variation of advanced methods such as the LEOR method. After solving the 2x2x3 in whatever method the solver wishes, there are just three more steps: PEC (originally called Pair + Edge + Corner), which finishes F2L-1 edge. Next use EBLE algorithms to solve the last F2L edge while orienting the last layer edges. Lastly finish the cube with ZBLL which contains 493 algorithms.

summary: PLL is the acronym for Permutation of the Last Layer. Permutation of the Last Layer is the last step of many speedsolving methods. In this step, the pieces on the top layer have already been oriented (OLL) so that the top face has all the same color, and they can now be moved into their solved positions. There are 21 PLLs (13 if you count mirrors and inverses as being the same) and each one is named after a letter.

title: Peridot
summary: In this step you find a corner from the bottom layer and put it in DBL position (done in inspection). After this you build a 2x2x2 block(like in Petrus) around the corner using only RrUuFf moves. Another way to put is once you have the corner in DBL, you solve the centers + BL edge + DL edge + DB edge. In this step you solve the dFL pair while solving edge orientation. This step is quite intuitive and easy. Although you could also do it using algorithms but those have not yet been generated.

title: Petrus Method
summary: The Petrus Method, invented by Lars Petrus, is a block-building method where the F2L is solved intuitively with no algorithms. Petrus used to be the second most popular speedcubing method behind Fridrich/CFOP; however nowadays it is often considered to be outdated as it has been steadily declining in popularity since the rise of the "Big Three" (CFOP, Roux and ZZ). Petrus-like Blockbuilding is sometimes partially used in CFOP solves for creating an XCross.

title: Philip Marshall
summary: Philip Marshall (or Phil Marshall) was a resident of Port Ludlow, Washington State, USA. In 1998 at around the age of 72, he published "The Ultimate Solution to Rubik's Cube" on the Internet. Intended for beginners, he referred to it as "a unique solution using only two series". It only requires 65 moves to solve a scrambled Rubik's Cube, although it is not well suited for advanced speedsolving. Marshall's solution is an Edges First solution.

title: Pikas**t
summary: Pikas**t (alternatively spelled sans asterisks) is a 3x3 speedsolving method proposed by Justin Harder on 24 June 2013 as a variant of the Petrus Method. Drawing influence from the Petrus and Roux methods, this method relies heavily on blockbuilding at the beginning of the solve and EO recognition at the end. thumb|upright|An example of pieces that can be solved in the C+OP step Build a 2x2x3 block anywhere on the cube. It is advised to consult the Petrus method for assistance.

title: Pizel method
summary: Pizel method  is a 3x3 method proposed by Alexandre Philiponet in 2011. Make a cross on the left side by solving all edges of a given color. Align the edges with the second-layer (M) centers. Place left corners (no orientation). As the cross is done in the left, this step is easily fingertrickable : < R, U, l > Put the first face on down (z') and then solve F2L. There are fewer cases than usual F2L since corners are already placed. francocube.com: - info on the method by the inventor

title: Portico
summary: The Portico Method is a 3x3 speedsolving method created by Matt DiPalma before 2017. It is derived from the ZZ Method, and the two share very much in common. The main difference is that ZZ's EOLine is replaced by EODB (the DF edge is omitted). Then, for the duration of the solve, the user is free to use F2 moves and the M'(U)M moves to solve F2L (which increases blockbuilding efficiency). The third step is COLL (42 algs). The final step is L5EP (16 algs), which solves all 4 LL edges and DF.

title: Pseudo Roux-Fop
summary: The Pseudo Roux-Fop method is a 3x3 speedsolving method developed by Tarun in 2025. It is designed for efficient solving with a blend of Roux-style blockbuilding and algorithmic last-layer techniques. The method typically averages around 55 moves per solve and leverages both intuition and pre-learned algorithms, making it a hybrid between intuitive solving and full-algorithmic execution. Build a 1x2x3 block on one side, but with the two corner pieces intentionally swapped.

title: Pure OLL
summary: Pure OLL is a 1LLL subset that solves for last layer cases which have all pieces correctly permuted, but not correctly oriented. Although it seems like a good subset to learn, recognition for Pure OLL cases are longer and harder to preform compared to OLL, ELL, etc.

title: Qipper method

summary: The Qipper Method is a 3×3 speedsolving method created by William Sallros in 2025. The method was designed as a simplified Last Layer approach where the solver permutes the entire top layer while simultaneously permuting a single corner from another layer. This reduces the number of required algorithms compared to methods like Ribbon method and ZB, while still providing efficient solves with minimal regrips.

title: Quadrangular Francisco
summary: The Quadrangular Francisco method is a speedsolving method created by Alex Yang, as a spin-off of the Hexagonal Francisco method invented by Andrew Nathenson. 1. Build a rectangle, which is a a 1x2x3 block, anywhere on the cube. 2. Rotate the cube so that you have the rectangle on either LD or RD (up to preference). The U layer should be completely free to move. Now, depending on what side the rectangle is on, use U and either R, Rw and M moves or L, Lw and M moves to solve the M slice.

title: RRBSP
summary: RRBSP (short for Reirto-RRNF's Belt, Separation and P3L) is a 3x3 method invented by Reirto-RRNF. This method was inspired by Belt, Square-1 Vandenbergh and ECP method 1. Pseudo EOBelt: Orient all edges while putting E layer edges to E layer 2. O8C: Orient all corners while preserving the Orientation and Belt. This step contains 191 algorithms.

title: RUP/PRUM/RUPM
summary: RUP or PRUM or RUPM (RU reduction, Pairs and Mirror reflection) method is a Blockbuilding method for the 3x3x3 cube proposed by Tsung-Yen Wu in 2018. The following describes the intended approach to RUPM, also known as RUP. PRUM is a similar, albeit slightly different method. The English tutorial for RUPM is outdated, and the Chinese tutorial details the intended approach. Build a 2x2x3 block, leaving the R and U faces free EO+CP.

title: RUbar
summary: RUbar is an experimental reduction method proposed by crystalcuber. It is a hybrid method, each major step is both moveset reduction and bandage reduction. The goal is to form 1x1x3 blocks called "bars" to progressively restrict the turning. At the end, the cube is reduced to the trivial <R2, U2> bandage. FB or 1x2x3 Block on left, reduced to <R, U M>

title: Ribbon Method

summary: The Ribbon Method is a speedsolving method created by Justin Taylor in 2017. The method was created as a Two-Look solution for the Last Slot and Last Layer without preorienting edges and maintaining a manageable algorithm count. This allows great versatility in approach for the F2L, along with a smooth transition into LSLL. The method retains every ergonomic advantage of CFOP, while containing one fewer "look" in the solve and saving an average of 6 moves with a CFOP-like approach to F2L.

title: Roux method
summary: Roux (French: [ʁu], English: [ɹuː] ROO) is a Rubik's cube speedsolving method invented by Gilles Roux. Roux is based on Blockbuilding and Corners First methods. It is notable for its low movecount, lack of rotations, heavy use of M moves in the last step, and adaptability to One-Handed Solving. 1. Build a 1x2x3 Block anywhere on the cube. 2. Build a second 1x2x3 block opposite of the first 1x2x3 block, without disrupting the first 1x2x3 block.

title: Russo method
summary: Russo is a method proposed by Anthony Russo in 2019. Russo is similar to Roux in the fact it is a blockbuilding method, but not similar in the way it solves BD edge, resulting in the final step only solving the last 5 edges instead of the last six. 1. Build the First 2 Layers without the FD cross edge. 2. Orient and Permute the Last Layer corners. 3a. Orient the remaining 5 edges. This step is done intuitively. 3b. Solve the last 5 edges in one algorithm.

title: SPL
summary: SPL is a method invented by Matilda Teixeira aka Matilda-Cruzzader25. The creator was inspired to make the method because of the fact that a team in the January 2021 Method Development Competition made one. EOSlice: Edges are oriented, while a line consisting of the DL and DR edges is formed. Pseudo F2B: The first two blocks (F2L, but missing the DF and DB edge) are built without regard to Corner Permutation. OCLL: The corners on the last layer are oriented. L6EP: Permute the last six edges.

title: SSC

summary: SSC, short for Shadowslice Snow Columns,(a variant with misoriented edges is called ECE), is a method that has variously been described as a variation on Orient First, an improved version of the Human Thistlethwaite Algorithm, an advanced Belt Method and a Columns first method.

title: SZ
summary: The SZ Method (Named after SZBLL) is a 3x3 speedsolving method invented by Nishan in 2026. It focuses on ergonomics and reduces the last layer algorithm count through a CO-based ZBLL step called SZBLL. The method name SZ stands for "Sized-down ZBLL." 3C: Solve DL, DR and DB edges. Similar to a the cross step on CFOP but without the last cross piece. F2L: Solve all four F2L pairs using M moves and keyhole techniques.

title: Salvia Method
summary: An experimental method by David Salvia. The novelty of his method is in the first two layers. 1. Adjacent middle-layer edges: RF and LF (3-4 moves) A variation of this 2LLL (2-look last layer), OLL then PLL could be used. ZBLL with edge control or M-CELL may also be used for the last layer.

title: Sandwich Method
summary: The Sandwich Method is a Cage variation based on Denny Dedmore's solution. Although the method was originally designed for big cubes, it can also be used to solve the 3x3, though it is just a CF method for the 3x3 version. Heavy center control at times during steps 6 and 7 are used (using different algorithms or other tricks), and Rachmaninovian currently uses a centers system that produces a ~4 look average. Java is needed to see his cube applets.

title: Seaweed Method
summary: The Seaweed Method is a variant of the Columns First Methods. It was mainly created for fun and isn't very efficient. It was inspired by several methods (such as CFOP, Columns First Methods, Reduction 3x3). You could also do this by solving the four first layer corners and then the four middle layer edges using the LBL alg and its mirror. This step is very easy to do intuitively, although you could use one of the four algorithms. Orient the four LL corners using at least 2-Look OLL.

title: Sexy Method

infobox.name: Sexy
infobox.variants: 8355, MirIS, Y-Move Method, Less is More

summary: Sexy Method is a variant of the 8355 Method specifically designed for ease of learning, using a single algorithm: the sexy move. Intuitively solve 3 of the E-slice edges, leaving a keyhole. Use the sexy move to solve the corresponding 3 D-layer corners by passing them from the U-layer through the keyhole. Solve the last 2 edges, using intuition or algorithms. Solve 3 more corners with the sexy move as before. To avoid confusion, leave the corner under the keyhole unsolved.

title: Sledgehog
summary: A method, proposed by Ryan Vigil in late 2017, based on tripod and sledgehammers. As a more intuitive method, it can be used to generate a good skeleton for FMC if steps are done loosely. 2. Build F2L-1. This step can be done as the first step, using blockbuilding 3. Finish tripod. This step is done intuitively. 4. Place the remaining three edges using up to 2 sledgehammer algorithms.

title: Slice Fransisco
summary: Slice Fransisco is a Rubik's cube method invented by Reddit user SciK3 and was named by Reddit user BanditTrain. The method uses aspects of the Roux method, Belt, and SSC. The method involves solving the E slice minus the F and B centers, creating two "bars" on the left and right sides, followed by orienting corners intuitively and permuting them using an alg set named UDC and a variation of LSE for edges. From that point on, the method solves like you would with Roux after 4a. 2a.

title: Snyder Method
summary: The Snyder Method, invented by Anthony Snyder in 1982, is both a fewest moves and a speedsolving method for the 3x3x3 cube. It is based on blockbuilding and can be compared to Petrus and the Heise Method. 1. (2x2x2 block step or Xcross step) Form a 2x2x2 block, optionally an Xcross. (Anthony has since added optional starts using a 1x2x3 or a 2x2x3, also with or without the cross.) 2. (Go to F2L-1 cube state) Use any variety of methods to solve the rest of F2L, except for one slot.

title: Speed Heise-2
summary: Speed Heise-2 is a intuitive 3x3 speedsolving method proposed by CriticalCubing and Teoidus in 2017. SH-2 offers an alternate speed optimized approach to normal Heise. It uses Speed-Heise algorithm set developed by Matt DiPalma for making the 5e2c step of Heise, speed optimized.

title: Square-101

infobox.name: Square-101
infobox.steps: 7 (EOEdge, CO setup, Belt+CO, D-pairs, L6CP, LR, M-Perm)

summary: Square-101 is a 3x3 method developed in the Method Development Competition August 2020. It won Best for FMC and Most Original Method. CO setup: Two 1x2x3 blocks on U and D where the top is an oriented square and pseudopair, and the bottom is all oriented. Belt+CO: Insert the pseudopair and orient the remaining corners on R (27 algs + 27 mirrors = 54 total, 7 moves) D-pairs: Create two corner and edge pairs on the D layer in the back.

title: TICT
summary: TICT is an experimental 3x3 method invented by Feliks Zemdegs in 2009. TICT stands for: Twins, Intuitive Corners, T perm. Twins step (also called 2 blocks 1x1x3 step) This step is often cut in 2 substeps: 1x1x3 Block and then second 1x1x3 Block. This step is fully intuitive. At the end of this step, we have the 1st Layer - 2 Opp Edg cube state. This step consists in solving the remaining corners intuitively. You may use one of the COLL algs or using the J-perm b alg (for instance).

title: TN
summary: TN (short for Tuan Ngo) is a 3x3 speedsolving method proposed by Ngô Anh Tuấn in 2025. It is inspired by ZZ-CT and is a two-look LSLL method like ZB, divided into TNLS and TNLL. TNLS solves the last slot edge and orients the last layer (except one last layer corner) by using VLS, OLL, or OLS-FE algorithms. Also, It is 100% possible to know in advance which subset of TNLL will appear from the TNLS step.

title: Thistlethwaite's algorithm
summary: A computer cube solving algorithm, based on reducing the cube to subgroups.

title: Triangular Francisco
summary: The Triangular Francisco method is a 3x3 speedsolving/novelty method invented on a whim by Michael Gottlieb when Thom Barlow posted an omegle conversation with a stranger who claimed to be able to solve a cube in 5 seconds with the "Triangular Francisco Method". The method was created in less than 20 minutes, yet still has a lot of potential to be fast. The method has not been explored very deeply yet.

summary: Tripod is a 1LLL subset that solves for last layer cases which have a 2x2x1 block.

title: Tripod Method

infobox.name: Tripod
infobox.proposers_raw: Ryan Heise, Michael Gottlieb, Mirek Goljan

summary: A blockbuilding approach to solving the 3x3x3, first proposed by Ryan Heise and developed by Michael Gottlieb and Mirek Goljan. The method is characterized by the final steps, which involve solving a 'tripod' composed of the three 1x1x2 columns connected to the URF corner piece. 1. Build a 2x2x2 block. This is an intuitive step. 2.Build 3 1x2x2 block side by side the 2x2x2 block. This is also an intuitive step. 4. Finish the last layer using one of 58 algorithms.

title: VDW method
summary: VDW, short for VanDerWyst, is a Rubik's cube speedsolving method proposed by Alex VanDerWyst in 2015. It could be described as a mix of Corners First and Roux and allows for high TPS while maintaining a low movecount and keeping blockbuilding to a minimum. In spite of its potential, it currently doesn't have any active users. Lines (sometimes also "Skis" or "Twins"): Two 1x1x3 blocks are built in DL and DR, respectively. Centers can be ignored here.

summary: VH (short for Vandenbergh-Harris) is a variant of the CFOP method invented by Lars Vandenbergh and Dan Harris. It orients the last layer edges during insertion of the final F2L block. It has exactly the same effect as the ZBLS stage of the ZB method, but uses much fewer algorithms - 32 VHLS algorithms as opposed to ZBLS's 125 (excluding mirrors and inverses).

title: WaterRoux
summary: WaterRoux is a Corners First method that is a hybrid of Waterman and Roux. Build a 1x2x3 block on the left as in Roux Solve the DFR and DBR corners in any permutation/orientation with at least one of them having the correct facelet on the D layer Solve all four remaining corners with either a CMLL, TCMLL, LEG-1 or TLEG-1 algorithm. Now the first block and all the corners are solved.

title: Waterman method
summary: The Waterman method is a method for solving the 3x3x3 cube which was invented by Marc Waterman in the 1980s. The method is based on Corners First methods but is efficient enough to be used for advanced speedsolving. The method was developed by Marc Waterman and his friend Daan Krammer in 1981. Marc added "a lot of additional processes and shortcuts" to achieve a sub-17-second average by the mid-1980s (Minh Thai's 1982 "world record" by comparison was 22.95 seconds).

summary: The Wilhelm method is a speedsolving method proposed by Jheris Ward. The Wilhelm method is a combination of the Roux and CFOP methods, considered by most to be the top 2 methods for speedsolving. This method combines steps from the Roux and CFOP methods. 1. Build a 1x2x3 Block anywhere on the cube. Once finished, hold this block on either the lower left or lower right side of the cube. 2. Repeat the first step on the opposite side of the cube, without breaking the first block.

title: Workbench
summary: For those new to the Rubik's cube this may help: A 3x3x3 cube is a regular geometrical object with 8 corners, 12 edges, 6 faces and 6 Centers. Cubie(s) are organized into Layer(s) or (more generally) 'Slice(s)' and Rotation(s) (also called 'move'(s), Each rotation identifies a slice (the cubies moved by the rotation). Rotations are organized in Algorithms (one of them is the 'Sledgehammer' used here). There are many strategies to solve the Rubik's cube, called Method(s) Practising the cube.

title: XG method
summary: XG (short for Xtreme-Garron) is a Rubik's cube solving method proposed by Lucas Garron in 2009. Make a cross on one side by solving all edges of a given color. Align the edges with the second-layer centers. You have to finish the 1st layer. For each of the 4 corners, you have to look after it on the 3rd layer and then insert it on the right place with the right orientation.

title: XLL
summary: XLL is a subset of 1LLL that solves the cases where all corners are oriented but not the edges. It's the last step of COALL after COLS. Opp flip (2 opposite edges misoriented, 40 cases) Adj flip (2 adjacent edges misoriented, 72 cases)

summary: The LBL-Y Method is a 3x3x3 beginner method. It is a layer-by-layer method with workspace similar to the 8355 Method and SAM. The basic design goal is to rely only on a single algorithm, the elementary commutator F R' F' R. The LBL-Y method shares the single-algorithm property with Less is More, which also uses F R' F' R,  and SAM, which like the 8355 Method uses the elementary commutator of type F R F' R'.

title: Yellow Bird

infobox.name: Yellow Bird
infobox.moves: ~53 moves (~30 for F2L + ~23 for OLL+PLL, although other approaches can also be used)

summary: Yellow Bird is a 3x3 method invented by nuclearaven in 2020 for the first Method Development Competition. The method is based on two core concepts: Low movecount, achieved through Blockbuilding, and <RUF> reduction using the F <RU> F' technique, which allows for a rotationless and ergonomic solve.

title: YruRU
summary: YruRU (pronounced Why-Roo-Roo) is a 3x3x3 method designed specifically for One-Handed Solving. It is a CP-first method that relies on reduced move-sets to ensure great ergonomics for OH turning. The name YruRU is said to stand for Yash's r-u-R-U reduction, but can also be interpreted as "Why Roux?", a dig on Roux, which is widely regarded as the optimal OH speedsolving method known.

title: ZB method
summary: ZB (short for Zborowski-Bruchem after its proponents, Zbigniew Zborowski and Ron van Bruchem) is a very efficient but algorithm-intensive method which is a variation of advanced LBL methods such as the Fridrich method.

title: ZBLL
summary: ZBLL is a step in many methods which involves solving the entire last layer in one step, assuming that the edges are already oriented. This is part of the ZB method, but it can be useful for any other method which leaves the edges of the last layer oriented after F2L is solved (such as the Petrus method, or ZZ Method). According to Zborowski's webpage, Bernard Helmstetter created the original algorithms for Lars Petrus, who proposed solving the last layer in one step.

title: ZBRoux

infobox.name: ZBRoux
infobox.proposers_raw: CriticalCubing (LLOB), Stachu Korick, Jules Manalang, James Straughan and Multiple others

summary: ZBRoux is a speedsolving method that uses a unique approach to solving the last 10 pieces in Roux, here, you solve the DF and DB edges while correcting edge orientation to achieve the F2L + EO cube state, and from there on, you finish the last layer in one look using ZBLL. It has been proposed numerous times dating back to 2010, so, the question of who gets credit is unclear. 1. First Block(FB): Build a 1x2x3 block anywhere on the cube.

title: ZCF
summary: ZCF is a method invented by Matilda Teixeira aka Matilda-Cruzzader. This method was inspired by Waterman, ZZ, ECP, Roux. COES: Orient corners while putting E Layer edges in the E Layer. Make sure to never have an E Layer edge in DF. The Edge Orientation step may be hard to get used to for beginners.

title: ZZ method
summary: The ZZ method is a 3x3 speedsolving method created by Zbigniew Zborowski in 2006. The method is focused both on low move count and high turning speed; during the majority of F2L, the solver only needs to make L, U, and R moves, which means that the solver's hands never leave the left and right sides of the cube, resulting in faster solving. In addition, edges are already oriented when the solver reaches the last layer, meaning the solver has fewer cases to deal with.

title: ZZ-CT
summary: ZZ-CT is a 3x3 method proposed by Chris Tran. It is a variant of the ZZ Method with a unique 2 look LSLL, divided into TSLE and TTLL. TSLE inserts the last edge whilst orienting all corners.

title: ZZ-EF
summary: ZZ-EF or ZZ-Edges First is a variant of the ZZ method proposed by Matt DiPalma in 2014. This variant aims to maximize the occurrence of skips and easy cases, increasing the chance of lucky and thus fast solves. EOLine: Like in ZZ, the solve starts by orienting all edges and creating a line. Lucky ZZ F2L: The first two layers are solved <RUL(D)>-gen.

title: ZZ-Mehta
summary: ZZ-Mehta is a variant of Mehta invented by metroidpine, who is also known on the SpeedSolving Forums under the alias obscurecuber. In the method, edges are oriented at the start of the solve like in ZZ, as opposed to standard Mehta, in which Edge Orientation is performed during the 3/4 Belt step. EO: All 12 edges are oriented like in ZZ. First Block: A 1x2x3 block is built on the bottom left. 3/4 Belt: 3/4 of a Belt are solved.

title: ZZ-Snake Pattern

infobox.name: ZZ-Snake Pattern

summary: The ZZ-Snake Pattern method is a 3x3 speedsolving method proposed by Zachary Olmoz and developed by Alex Maass, in 2016. The method is focused both on low move count and high turning speed; during the majority of F2L, the solver only needs to make L, U, and R moves, which means that the solver's hands never leave the left and right sides of the cube, resulting in faster solving.

title: ZZ-blah
summary: ZZ-blah is a variation of ZZ proposed by Chester Lian in which the last-layer corners are disoriented during insertion of the last F2L block to reduce the last layer to only the pi and H cases. Because it can only give two OLL cases, the last layer can be solved in one look with 133 algorithms.

title: ZZLL
summary: The Zbigniew Zborowski Last Layer is the subset of ZBLL in which two opposite LL edges are correctly permuted. It is used to solve the last layer in the ZZ-b variant of the ZZ Method. Compared with ZBLL's 494 cases, ZZLL has only 169 distinct cases which can be completed with a minimum of 80 algorithms assuming mirrors and inverses are used. ZZLL also serves as a useful transition between COLL/EPLL and full ZBLL.

title: Zagorec method
summary: The Zagorec method is a 3x3 method created by Damjan Zagorec in 2012. The following steps describe an approach suited for beginners, more advanced users might combine steps 4 and 5 and for 7 and 8 steps  use a Fridrich type last layer and do PLL.

summary: The Zipper Method is a speedsolving method created by Justin Taylor in 2017, several months after development of the Ribbon Method. The method was created as a Two-Look solution for the Last Slot and Last Layer without preorienting edges and maintaining a manageable algorithm count. This allows great versatility in approach for the F2L, along with a smooth transition into LSLL.
